verdict.rationale: The evidence pack contains nothing about how Lowenstein Sandler uses AI in client service: no named AI tools, no AI-use policies, and no proprietary AI-practice products. The Clerky partnership is a document and formation workflow platform with no AI described, and the llms.txt file only makes the firm's website readable by AI agents. Neither shows AI use in client service, so both are adjacent at best. This is a fair question to ask of a law firm, so the absence of evidence means none rather than na.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, the firm publishes how it uses AI in client service — named tools, policies, or AI-practice products of its own — beyond a marketing mention
